description: Constant-product bonding curve with virtual quote liquidity: buys, sells, progress-dependent sell-side burn, terminal disposition burn, threshold crossing, and boundary cases.

units.meme: atomic units, 9 decimals in these cases
units.quote: atomic units, 9 decimals in these cases

rounding.meme_out_net: gross meme output minus meme fee

parameters.note: Every value here is proposed, not accepted, and sourced from docs/decisions/0004-bonding-curve.md (curve and LaunchConfig-owned asset fees), docs/decisions/0003-treasury-cap-lifetime-and-burn.md (max_burn_bps) and docs/decisions/0006-fees-and-launch-paths.md (migration fee and its ceiling). Changing one invalidates every case below.

formulas.buy: quote_fee=ceil(q*quote_fee_bps/10000); q_net=q-quote_fee; meme_gross=floor(M*q_net/(V+Q+q_net)); meme_fee=ceil(meme_gross*meme_fee_bps/10000); meme_net=meme_gross-meme_fee; M'=M-meme_gross; Q'=Q+q_net
formulas.sell: meme_fee=ceil(m*meme_fee_bps/10000); m_after_fee=m-meme_fee; progress_bps=min(floor(Q*10000/T),10000); burn_bps=floor(max_burn_bps*progress_bps/10000); burned=ceil(m_after_fee*burn_bps/10000); eff=m_after_fee-burned; gross=floor((V+Q)*eff/(M+eff)); quote_fee=ceil(gross*quote_fee_bps/10000); net=gross-quote_fee; M'=M+eff; Q'=Q-gross

cases.name: buy_first_one_quote_unit
cases.notes: Opening trade against virtual liquidity only.

cases.name: buy_meme_fee_only
cases.notes: A zero quote rate and positive meme rate select meme-only fees.

cases.name: buy_both_asset_fees
cases.notes: Positive rates in both assets charge each fee exactly once.

cases.name: sell_mid_with_progress_burn
cases.notes: Burn moment 1 at partial progress. quote_out_gross <= real_quote holds without a clamp.

cases.name: sell_both_asset_fees
cases.notes: Meme fee precedes the burn and curve; quote fee follows the curve.

cases.name: buy_to_below_threshold
cases.notes: Fresh sequence. Stops just below the terminal threshold.

cases.name: buy_crossing_threshold
cases.notes: Crossing happens on a buy only. Terminal state feeds the migration price.

cases.name: sell_at_full_progress_max_burn_unreachable
cases.notes: Pure-math boundary, UNREACHABLE through the lifecycle. progress_bps reaches 10000 only when real_quote >= T, and crossing T closes trading, so no sell can execute in this state. Retained to pin the arithmetic at the top of the ramp; it must never be presented as an executable trade. See the sell_at_max_live_progress case for the highest burn a live sell can actually incur.

cases.name: sell_at_max_live_progress
cases.notes: Highest burn attainable on an executable sell: real_quote = T-1 gives progress_bps 9999 and burn_bps 99, one basis point below the configured max_burn_bps of 100. The state is constructed directly rather than reached by a buy, because the ceiling fee makes the net-quote map non-surjective and no single gross amount yields net exactly T-1; the sell function is a pure function of state, so the vector is well-defined regardless.

cases.name: sell_round_trip_immediately_after_first_buy
cases.notes: Inverse/dust bound. Spent 1000000000, recovered 980099999; 19900001 lost, of which 1 atomic unit is curve-retained rounding dust and 19900000 is the two fees. progress_bps is 3, which floors to burn_bps 0 - the ramp does not round a negligible progress up into a burn.

cases.name: buy_one_atomic_unit
cases.notes: One atomic quote unit is entirely consumed by the ceiling fee. A zero-output trade must abort with a named error, not succeed silently.

cases.name: sell_more_meme_than_exists_outside_curve
cases.notes: Unreachable in practice: no meme exists outside the curve at M0, so no caller can hold this Coin<Meme>. Recorded because it is exactly the state in which the historical .min() clamp would bind. Blast asserts the sell-back invariant instead of clamping.

cases.name: terminal_disposition

expect.burn_moment_2_rule: meme_available_for_liquidity minus meme actually deployed by the venue adapter is burned in one accounted step before the supply state is locked to BurnOnly

cases.notes: Burn moment 2. The exact burned amount depends on how much meme the venue consumes at the derived price, so the rule is asserted rather than a fixed number.

properties.name: sell_back_invariant
properties.statement: For any gross meme input not exceeding the user's net meme received from reachable buys, quote_out_gross <= real_quote.
properties.status: backed by sui/launchpad/tests/curve_tests.move at fixed seed 314159 over 256 reachable buy-then-sell scenarios cycling through no fees, quote-only, meme-only, and both
properties.evidence: Every scenario sells the complete purchased Meme amount and one generated partial amount. The test commits its generator, fee modes, parameters, seed, operation count, an algebraically equivalent pre-call check, and an assert_eq trace that prints the operation index plus all generated/state inputs on failure.

properties.name: monotonicity
properties.statement: At fixed fee rates, meme_out_net is non-decreasing in quote_in and non-increasing in real_quote.

properties.name: conservation_meme_atomic_units
properties.statement: before migration: meme_total_supply_initial = M + meme_outstanding + accrued_fees_meme + meme_named_claims + pending_burn + meme_deployed_to_venue; after migration pending_burn becomes burned_terminal
properties.note: Burn appears only in this identity. Meme and quote are never combined into one equation.

properties.name: conservation_quote_atomic_units
properties.statement: quote_in_total = quote_out_total + Q + accrued_fees_quote + quote_named_claims + migration_fee_quote + quote_deployed_to_venue

properties.name: burn_ramp_top_is_an_asymptote
properties.statement: burn_bps == max_burn_bps requires progress_bps == 10000, which requires real_quote >= T, at which point trading is closed. The maximum burn on an executable sell is max_burn_bps - 1.

properties.name: intermediate_width
properties.statement: All products and effective-reserve sums widen to u256. Buy output is bounded by M, sell output is checked against Q before narrowing, and post-trade u64 reserve additions are checked.
